title: KV: Pinned Hotspot Steward and Cooperative Spill Shepherd (fragment-aware eviction)
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a pinned-hotspot region and background compaction (non-blocking) plus a cooperative spill scheduler to reduce fragmentation-driven paging and smooth spill I/O. Improves tail latency and reduces memory churn under hotspot workloads.
description: Context: Production traces show recurring latency spikes and high spill I/O when a small fraction of tenant keys experience bursty write/read hotness, causing frequent micro-evictions and fragment churn in the KV in-memory cache. Motivation: Reduce fragmentation and repeated alloc/dealloc churn for hot keys while avoiding large stop-the-world compactions that violate latency SLOs. Design summary: 1) Pinned Hotspot Steward: tenant-local lightweight region allocator to pin small groups of frequently-accessed entries into a compact hot region. Pinning is not permanent: entries get a temperature score and are demoted when cooled. 2) Cooperative Background Mender: a low-priority background worker that performs gentle in-place compaction of fragmented buckets/segments using incremental, preemptible passes integrated with the request scheduler to avoid latency interference. 3) Spill Shepherd: coordinated spill sequencer that batches spill-to-disk/network operations across tenants and rate-limits I/O to avoid bursty spill storms; includes prioritized ordering so cold but large objects spill earlier while small hot objects are retained when possible. 4) Fragment-aware eviction policy: hybrid SLRU + size-temperature heuristic that biases eviction away from pinned hotspots and prefers high-fragmentation candidates for reclamation. 5) Kernel & scheduling hooks: added a small set of hints for the serving runtime scheduler so batch windows avoid picking worker threads currently doing mender passes; KV operations expose light-weight contended-region metrics to the kernel to better schedule continuous batching windows. Commits: feat(kv): add pinned-hotspot steward and temperature scoring; feat(kv/mender): background mender engine with preemptible passes; feat(kv/spill): spill shepherd orchestration and rate-limiter; perf(kv): fragment-score calculation and policy integration; ci: end-to-end smoke + canary for hotspot workload; docs: operator notes and rollout plan. Files changed (high-level): src/kv/pinned_steward.rs, src/kv/mender.rs, src/kv/spill_shepherd.rs, src/kv/eviction_policy.rs, src/runtime/scheduler_hints.rs, tests/kv/hotspot_integration.rs, examples/bench/hotspot_stress.toml, docs/ops/kv-hotpatch.md, ci/canary-hotspot.yml. Benchmarks: In our 99th percentile latency canary (multitenant hotspot stress with 10% keys hot at 10x base QPS), results vs main baseline: 99p reduced from 180ms -> 120ms (33% improvement), average memory overhead +6% for pinned regions, overall downstream spill IOPS reduced 45%. End-to-end throughput sustained at parity with baseline; slight improvement in tail throughput under load. Testing and validation: unit tests for temperature demotion and pin/unpin semantics, integration test that replays production hotspot trace (tests/kv/hotspot_replay.py), canary rollout with staged config (25% -> 100% of traffic) and real-time observer dashboards to validate fragmentation score trends. Rollout notes: default pinning enabled for workloads with >1% repeated-key hotness; operator controls: pin-size-limit, mender-burst-ms, spill-rate-limit. Backwards compatibility: safe defaults avoid pinning on memory constrained hosts; no surface API changes. Merge: squash-merged after two approvals and CI green. Related work: follows ENG-2045 (memory-profiling) and ENG-2102 (spill orchestration).

review_comments: Arjun Patel (2024-11-01): Generally LGTM but please add metrics for pinned-region occupancy and per-tenant pin counts.
Maya Chen (2024-11-01): Added metrics and dashboard panels; updated docs with limits and tuning knobs.
Lucía Morales (2024-11-03): Mender preemption looks good but add a safety net to stop compaction if ongoing latency breaches SLO (added guard).
Benji Kim (2024-11-04): Verified canary runs; observed reduction in spill IOPS. Minor nits around logging levels addressed.
QA (2024-11-05): End-to-end canary at 50% for 4h with no regression; will proceed to full rollout.
Maya Chen (2024-11-06): Squashed and addressed final test flake; ready to merge.
notes_on_benchmark: Canary workload: hotspot-10pct-10x. 99p latency drop 33%, spill IOPS down 45%. Memory overhead due to pinned region ~6% but translates to lower overall IO cost and improved 99p latency. Observed no regression in throughput. Detailed benchmark scripts added under examples/bench.
how_to_revert: Revert squash commit a3d9b4f17c8e6b2d5f9c4a2b6e0f1c3d9b8a7f4c if a rollback is needed. Operator knob 'pin_enabled=false' also disables behavior without code revert.
operator_notes: Default configuration is conservative: pin_size_limit=16KiB per-tenant, mender_burst_ms=50, spill_rate_limit=100MB/s cluster-wide. Monitoring: kv.pinned.region.occupancy, kv.fragmentation.score, kv.spill.rate, runtime.batch.preemptions.
known_issues: Edge case: workloads with extremely high-cardinality ephemeral hot keys may see limited benefit; operator should disable pinning for that tenant. Initial implementation does not compact pinned regions aggressively; future iteration will add in-place shrink for long-lived hotspots.
ci_log_snippet: CI: unit-tests passed (128/128), integration hotspot_replay passed, canary smoke passed. Lint: minor style warnings fixed. All checks green at merge.
migration_steps: No DB schema changes. Operators should stage canary on a non-critical shard, monitor fragmentation score trends for 24-48h, then expand rollout. Config knobs exist in config/kv-hotpatch.yaml.
